subject: Art & Design
title: Documentary Photography: Truth in Frames
description: A 60-second lesson on Documentary Photography: Truth in Frames.

hook.text: Dorothea Lange's 'Migrant Mother' showed America what the Great Depression looked like. Policy changed.

buildup.text: Documentary photography records real events as they happen, without staging or manipulation.

discovery.text: Its power lies in credibility. Viewers trust that what they see actually happened.

twist.text: Digital manipulation blurs the line. News agencies now require unedited RAW files to verify authenticity.

climax.text: From war zones to climate change, documentary photos create empathy that statistics never can.

punchline.text: One authentic photo can do what a thousand words can't.

quiz.question: Why do news agencies require unedited RAW files from photographers?
options: To verify the photo hasn't been digitally manipulated
RAW files are smaller in size

details.summary: Documentary photography uses images to record reality, tell stories, and bear witness to events, conditions, and cultures. From Dorothea Lange's Depression-era portraits to Sebastião Salgado's global labor documentation, the genre aims to inform, educate, and inspire change through visual truth.
details.whyItMatters: Documentary photography carries moral authority that other genres lack — it says 'this really happened.' This power to bear witness has driven social change, from civil rights to environmental awareness, making photography a force for justice.
takeaways: Documentary photography records reality and bears witness
Lange and Salgado used images to drive social awareness
The genre carries moral authority as visual evidence

faq.question: How is documentary photography different from photojournalism?
faq.answer: Photojournalism covers specific news events on deadline. Documentary photography explores broader themes over longer periods — sometimes years. A photojournalist photographs a flood; a documentary photographer spends months documenting a community's recovery.

faq.question: Can documentary photography be staged?
faq.answer: The genre's ethical standards generally prohibit staging. Some of its greatest controversies involve discovered staging — certain Dorothea Lange and Robert Capa images were questioned.
